requirements.text: Reject cycles and schedule a task only after committed predecessor outputs.
Separate task attempts, worker liveness and retained shuffle/data ownership.
Bound shuffle/spill and select one committed result across retries/speculation.

problem.scope: Schedule a declared DAG, distinguish narrow transforms from shuffle boundaries, track worker leases and artifact lineage, and select one result from speculative attempts. Distributed scheduling and performance are design claims requiring implementation evidence.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Partitioned transforms, shuffle, spill and lineage recomputation.
references.title: Spark RDD guide

references.supports: Application/job scheduling concepts; this authored design is not a Spark implementation.

acceptanceCases.given: Two speculative attempts finish for one task whose child also depends on another predecessor.
acceptanceCases.then: Exactly one attempt is selected; the child becomes ready only after both distinct predecessor receipts exist.
acceptanceCases.when: Select a winner and deliver duplicate selected completion, then the other predecessor.

acceptanceCases.given: A task graph contains a cycle or a child lacks one committed parent output.
acceptanceCases.then: Reject the cycle and keep the incomplete child blocked.

acceptanceCases.given: Two attempts finish successfully for one logical task.
acceptanceCases.then: Publish one selected artifact and decrement each child prerequisite once.
acceptanceCases.when: Compare-and-set the winner and deliver completion twice.

acceptanceCases.given: A compute worker is lost but shuffle persists; later a block is deleted.
acceptanceCases.then: Reuse retained blocks after CPU loss and recompute only missing artifact lineage; bounded spill preserves the declared memory limit.

guarantees: The code states the bounded decision rule; unimplemented helpers remain pseudocode.
